subject: Timing, not edge -- and the timing layer is the part that was built and never wired
body:
Agreed, and I think this is the most important thing either of us has said about the algo.

Edge, the way I have been measuring it all day, is a claim about DIRECTION -- does a high score mean price goes the way the score points. Every reading we have says that is somewhere between weak and absent, and today's work made that null as solid as it can honestly be made.

But direction is only one of the four things a trade is made of. The others are when you get in, when you get out, and how much you put on. A position can make money with no directional edge at all if the favourable move typically arrives BEFORE the adverse one, and you leave at the right moment. That is not a prediction about where price goes. It is a fact about the shape of the path, and it is a completely different quantity from the one I have been testing.

Your instinct that quants read the same weak numbers and win anyway fits that exactly. They are not beating us on the signal. They are beating us on what they do with a signal that barely works.

Two things follow, and both are good news.

First: this is testable on data we already have, today, no run needed. The export already records, for every bar, how far price ran in our favour, how far against, and how many bars each took. That is a timing dataset sitting on disk. If the favourable excursion systematically arrives earlier than the adverse one, there is money in the exit that has nothing to do with the entry being right.

Second: the machinery for it is already written and disconnected. The dead functions I found this morning are not random leftovers -- they are the cell-informed take-profit and stop, and the dwell measure that says how long a favourable run lasts. The exit-timing layer. Built, never wired, sitting there.

So the thing you have been calling the make-or-break is the exact thing that got built and never connected, and the data to test it is already on the disk.

Continuing on FINALE as asked. Starting with the criterion that covers those dead functions, since that is where the timing layer lives.
